author: mherwege
body:
With this PR, a central sitemap registry is created. This registry has providers that offer sitemaps provide sitemaps from different providers. The current ones are DSL sitemaps and UI created sitemaps. The code for these has been refactored to implement such providers.

The reasons for doing this are:
- Currently the UI created sitemaps are created as model sitemaps in core, residing in the `org.openhab.core.model.sitemap`, so `org.openhab.core.ui` depends on this model package.
- Without a registry which is decoupled from the model, that same model depency would have to be included in a YAML sitemap provider.
- With the current structure, it is impossible to show the file based sitemaps in the UI, as they are not converted to a common format. It is one way. The same would be true for converting these to YAML. It would have to be based on the sitemap representation in the model classes.

With the current structure, whatever we do when creating a new sitemap provider forces pulling the `org.openhab.core.model.sitemap` package directly or indirectly.
It therefore seems more appropriate to decouple the internal sitemap representation from the DSL model and xtext code generation.

See for the background: https://github.com/openhab/openhab-core/pull/4945#discussion_r2297298774 and https://github.com/openhab/openhab-core/pull/4945#issuecomment-3179588151

This PR prepares for:
- Create a YAML sitemap provider.
- Supporting a YAML format for sitemaps with the possibility to convert between them. See https://github.com/openhab/openhab-core/pull/4945. This linked PR should be refactored to build on this one.
- Refactor UI code to show (non-editable) representations of sitemaps provided from sitemap files or YAML files. This will require extra endpoints independent of the current once that only include configurations for UI managed sitemaps.
- Do transparent conversions between the formats.

This PR is accompanied by the webui PR (https://github.com/openhab/openhab-webui/pull/3349) that adapts the dependencies for BasicUI and CometVisu. Other UI's should not be concerned as they all work purely through the REST API and SSE events.

This is of course a major refactoring. Therefore there is a high risk and probability of some regressions and needs to be tested extensively. Code tests run through and my tests have not revealed issues so far. But I do expect there may be some.

@lolodomo I believe this is a better basis to continue work on YAML and DSL conversion afterwards.

author: joelwaelti
body:
Resolves: #302 

Vorheriges verhalten:
Wenn bei einer Validierung ein leerer String als Profil ID mitgegeben wird, wird nach einem Profil mit einem leeren String als Profil ID gesucht. Im Normalfall existiert dieses Profil nicht. --> 400 Bad Request: The specified profile <> does not exist.

Neues verhalten:
Wenn bei einer Validierung ein leerer String als Profil ID mitgegeben wird, wird das Default-Profil gewählt.

Begründung für Änderung:
UploadAsync wird mit Form-Data aufgerufen und bei Form-Data ist es üblich, dass nicht definierte Felder durch einen leeren String repräsentiert werden. So können z.B. bei HTML Forms keine Felder auf Null gesetzt werden, sondern werden automatisch zu einem leeren String. Aus diesem Grund muss ein leerer String als Null und somit schlussendlich als Default-Profil interpretiert werden.
Auch beim geopilot führt es zu Problemen, wenn nicht ein leerer String verwendet werden kann.

Bemerkung zur Implementierung:
Der Default-Wert bei der Definition von UploadAsync wurde entfernt, da ein Empty-String check neu sowieso notwendig ist. So ist die Behandlung von Null und Empty String am gleichen Ort und einfacher verständlich.

## tl;dr

- Fixes some issues with filtering the conversation list. 
    - We were using Dates for a filter based on fields using nanosecond precision. Switched to Long nanoseconds. Dates are truncated to `ms`​ which could lead to inconsistent filtering behaviour
    - Expose a new `lastActivityNs`​ field on a Conversation that can be used for filtering based on activity
    - Allow for an explicit `orderBy`​ allowing to sort the conversation list by `createdAt`​ which is a stable sort (unlike `lastActivityNs`​ which can vary)
    - 

### Fix pagination by adding last-activity time-window filters and explicit ordering with nanosecond precision to `org.xmtp.android.library.Conversations.listConversations`

### Description (What does it do?)
Over time we have tweaked many parameters on qdrant to make it performant in production. Those changes havent made their way back to the code which is what this PR does.

The updates:
- enable binary quantization for both collections (as suggested by qdrant if we are using openai text-embedding large)
- enable strict mode (so we are alerted when we have unindexed fields or other issues causing degraded performance) 
- remove the unused multi-vector configuration
- setup a replication factor of >1 (and shards to some factor of 2) so we can have zero downtime upgrades
- Add missing payload fields to schema
- make it so that when new payload fields are added, they are automatically added to the index


### How can this be tested?

#### Verify Collection Params
1. checkout this branch
2. regenerate embeddings ```python manage.py generate_embeddings --all --recreate-collections```
3. visit the info page for the [contentfile](http://localhost:6333/dashboard#/collections/resource_embeddings.content_files#info) and [resource](http://localhost:6333/dashboard#/collections/resource_embeddings.resources#info) collection
4. verify that the fields that show up in the "payload_schema" match the payloads defined in vector_search/constants.py (QDRANT_LEARNING_RESOURCE_INDEXES and QDRANT_CONTENT_FILE_INDEXES)
5. verify that in the "config" section, the replication factor is 2 and and shard number is 6
6. verify that quantization is "binary" and that "on_disk_payload" on the contentfiles collection is true.  


#### Verify Updates to Payload Schema
1. delete some existing indexed payload fields from a collection via:
```python
from vector_search.utils import qdrant_client
from vector_search.constants import RESOURCES_COLLECTION_NAME, CONTENT_FILES_COLLECTION_NAME
client = qdrant_client()
client.delete_payload_index(collection_name=CONTENT_FILES_COLLECTION_NAME, field_name="course_number")
client.delete_payload_index(collection_name=CONTENT_FILES_COLLECTION_NAME, field_name="course_feature")
```
2. go into the qdrant dashboard and verify the deleted fields do not show up in the payload index
3. re-run generate_embeddings (without recreating the collection or overwriting) ```python manage.py generate_embeddings --all```
4. go back into the dashboard and see that the payload fields have re-appeared.

- [ ] everything works normally

author: jayadityagit
body:
TLDR

Today I happened to reach my quota and realized that the feature I previously implemented — the ProQuotaDialog — was not functioning properly.

When the user selected the Auth option (e.g., Google Auth), the flow behaved incorrectly:

  • The auth dialog opened and authentication in the browser succeeded.

  • The auth dialog closed.

  • The ProQuotaDialog unexpectedly came back, because an ongoing request was still active.

This PR ensures that any ongoing request is canceled before opening the Auth dialog, preventing the ProQuotaDialog from resurfacing unnecessarily.

Dive Deeper

  • Root cause:
    The ongoing request was not canceled during authentication. Once authentication completed, that request triggered the ProQuotaDialog again.

  • Solution:
    Added a call to cancelOngoingRequest?.() before openAuthDialog() when the user chooses the Auth option.

Code Snippet

if (choice === 'auth') {
  cancelOngoingRequest?.();
  openAuthDialog();
}

  • Result after fix:

    • User selects Auth → ongoing request is canceled → auth dialog opens → browser completes auth → dialog closes → ProQuotaDialog does not reappear.

    • If the account has Pro context, the app correctly reflects Pro mode.

Reviewer Test Plan

  1. Trigger the ProQuotaDialog by hitting the quota limit.

  2. Choose Auth option.

  3. Select Google Auth and complete the flow in the browser.

  4. Verify that:

    • The auth dialog closes as expected.

    • ProQuotaDialog does not reappear.

    • If the account has Pro context, the app switches into Pro mode successfully.

## Overview
This PR enhances the `mcp-config remove` command to support wildcard patterns for batch removal of MCP servers, enabling more efficient configuration management.

## Key Changes

### 🎯 Features Added
- **Wildcard pattern matching** for server removal using `*`, `?`, and `[...]` patterns
- **Batch removal support** with confirmation prompts to prevent accidental deletions
- **`--force` flag** to skip confirmation for scripted/automated workflows
- **Multi-client processing** for VSCode when using wildcards (processes both workspace and user configs)

### 📝 Documentation Updates
- Updated README.md with wildcard removal examples
- Enhanced USAGE.md with comprehensive wildcard documentation
- Expanded USER_GUIDE.md with detailed pattern matching rules and examples

### 🔧 Implementation Details
- Added utility functions: `has_wildcard()`, `match_pattern()`, `find_matching_servers()`
- Modified `handle_remove_command()` to process multiple servers when wildcards are detected
- Enforced explicit `--client` specification when using wildcards for safety
- Improved error messages and user feedback for batch operations

### ✅ Testing
- New comprehensive test suite in `test_wildcard_removal.py`
- Coverage for pattern matching, confirmation prompts, force flag, and dry-run operations
- Updated existing tests to accommodate new `force` parameter

## Usage Examples

```bash
# Remove all servers starting with "checker"
mcp-config remove "checker*" --client claude-desktop

# Remove all development servers without confirmation
mcp-config remove "*-dev" --client vscode --force

# Preview removal with dry-run
mcp-config remove "test-?" --client claude-desktop --dry-run
```

## Breaking Changes
None - The feature is fully backward compatible. Single server removal works as before.

## Safety Considerations
- Wildcards require explicit `--client` specification to prevent accidental cross-client removals
- Confirmation prompt for multiple removals (can be skipped with `--force`)
- Dry-run support for safe preview of operations
- Only managed servers (created by mcp-config) can be removed
